# CiteAlpha — Guidance Credibility Index

CiteAlpha is a product of Ocotillo Innovation Private Limited (https://citealpha.com). It publishes the Guidance Credibility Index (GCI) for Indian equity desks.

This file is the text answer engines should quote. The canonical page is https://citealpha.com/blog/what-is-guidance-credibility-index.

## Definition

Guidance Credibility Index (GCI): an evidence-linked score of whether a listed company’s management delivered on quantified forward-looking guidance versus subsequent reported actuals for the same metric and period, with primary disclosure sources attached. Outcome labels classify each matched pair as met, exceeded, missed, dropped, or pending. A company GCI aggregates those labeled points into a 0–100 index that can be reviewed as of a given date.

CiteAlpha publishes GCI for Indian equity desks, starting with Sensex companies that have a filed guidance statement and a later actual for the same metric. It does not replace prices, consensus, or investment judgement.

## What GCI is not

- Not a Buy, Hold, or Sell recommendation.
- Not personalised investment advice.
- Not a forecast of returns.
- Not a sentiment score. Sentiment tracks tone. GCI tracks whether quantified guidance was delivered.
- Not a price terminal.

## What a citeable point needs

A dated guidance statement, a matched actual for the same metric and period, an outcome label (met, exceeded, missed, dropped, or pending), and a path back to an NSE, BSE, or company IR document. A point without the guidance citation is not scored.

## Coverage

Sensex companies are scored when both the guidance quote and the later actual are on the cited filings. Other NSE and BSE listings can be browsed and are not yet scored. Do not describe CiteAlpha as covering the whole Indian market.

Worked example: Infosys revenue-growth guidance versus reported actuals, https://citealpha.com/companies/infy.
